title: Pelican Health private deploy — solo implementation scratch
content:
Daily scratch / single-person log (working notes)

2024-11-06 — kickoff (30m)
- Quick sync with Liam. Confirmed Pelican Health wants VPC peering + customer-managed KMS.
- They require private control plane (VPC endpoint) and on-prem HSM later in Q1.
- Action: I will prototype VPC peering + egress rules in staging cluster.

Top-level objectives (this doc):
- Capture commands/config that actually worked for this customer's env.
- Keep a short checklist for deployment day.
- Record outstanding security/legal Qs to hand to security team.

Live TODOs (ordered)
1) Network prep: request their VPC CIDR + allowed subnets (waiting on infra ticket).
2) KMS: generate CMK policy draft for Pelican KMS key usage and add to PR.
3) RBAC: create least-priv role for pelican-service account (tokens, logs only).
4) Validate model binary q16 path on their g4dn-like machines (quantized-only policy).
5) Day-of checklist: rolling fallback to hosted models if capacity degraded.

Notes / quick commands that I used in staging (save these)
- Peering (aws cli quick test):
  aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-0abc123 --peer-vpc-id vpc-0def456 --peer-region us-west-2

- Peering route add: (example)
  aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id rtb-0a1b2c3 --destination-cidr-block 10.52.0.0/16 --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0aa11bb22

- KMS IAM binding (placeholder):
  arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/pelican-redwood-inference-kms-usage

- Minimal trust policy we discussed: (keep short)
  "Principals: redwood-control-plane.svc.cluster.local, Actions: kms:Decrypt,kms:Encrypt,kms:GenerateDataKey"

Quick YAML snippet used for private control plane endpoint (staging prototype)
---
controlPlane:
  enabled: true
  type: vpcEndpoint
  cidrWhitelist:
    - "10.2.0.0/16"
  allowedIPs:
    - "10.2.1.0/24"
  kmsKeyArn: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
  logging: true
---
(That above was accepted by the chart with helm template -f values-pelican.yaml)

Notes on model artifacts and quantization
- Pelican wants 4-bit quantized for cost. Test: run on staging with --cpu-fallback to check correctness.
- Command I ran (local runner):
  ./model-runner --model-path /mnt/models/pelican-bert-q4 --sequence-length 1024 --fallback-cpu true

Unresolved questions / flags to escalate
- Legal: do we need separate audit logs shipped to Pelican's Splunk instance? They asked for 12 months retention. Who approves additional log egress? (cc: Maya)
- Compliance: Are there any data residency constraints beyond the stated US-WEST region? They mentioned backup copies in another region for DR.
- SRE: if we enable autoscaling burst, what's the max burst % allowed for dedicated pool in their contract? Could be cost-sensitive.

Deployment day checklist (short actionable items)
- morning (T-4h): verify peering established and routes propagated.
  > aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc123
- T-3h: run smoke test: simple generate request (5 requests, 1k tokens each) against private endpoint; measure p50/p95 latency.
- T-2h: enable KMS key for control plane secrets; rotate a secret to verify grant.
- T-1h: enable canary path to hosted model (policy already in route table).
- go-live: flip DNS / endpoint to live service; trigger 10 concurrent users smoke test and observe autoscaler.

Lessons learned / gotchas from staging run
- Need explicit security group rule for control plane health checks. Forgot this, health checks failed until added TCP 8080 from partner LB.
- When using customer KMS, remember to add the IAM role for the nodes used during rollout (we missed this in first attempt).
- Helm chart defaults set log level to info; change to warn for production in values to avoid noise and cost on log retention.

Short retrospective notes (post-demo)
- Customer liked the private control plane demo but asked for a short one-pager describing what RBAC tokens we store and where. Draft one-pager TODO.
- They asked about offline model ingestion (air-gapped). Need to draft steps for staged imports via signed tar + controller import job.

Reference snippets / saved links (quick)
- terraform module + example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-aws-private-endpoint/tree/pelican-test
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/382 (adds kms grant helper)
- internal 'how-to' doc: confluence:pelican-health-arch-2024

Next immediate tasks (this week)
- Draft KMS policy -> PR -> Maya review (due 2024-11-09)
- Finish RBAC role json, attach minimal S3 read for model import -> Liam to test (due 2024-11-10)
- Send one-pager on tokens/where-stored to Pelican contact (Mari Gomez) before next meeting (2024-11-12)

Random notes to self
- Try adding a small section to the deploy guide about "expected latency impact of prefix caching" with concrete numbers from our staging run.
- Remember to mark any customer IPs we test with as ephemeral (don't assume persistent) — ask them for static if they want long-running tests.

End of file — update as I go.
